newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Berdan Tekstil to float shares this week.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Berdan Tekstil to float shares this week.

text.p: Turkish textile producer Berdan Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. said it would issue 100 billion lira of new shares in a two-day offer starting from March 20.
The price per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share is fixed at 12,500 lira, the company said in a newspaper announcement.
The company will waive 100 billion lira of pre-emptive rights to increase its capital to 520 billion lira from 420 billion by offering the shares to the public.

The consortium that will manage the offer is led by ABN Amro Hoare Govett Istanbul securities and includes Vakif Investment, Demir Investment, Inter Investment, Nurol securities, Global securities, Eczacibasi Securities and Alfa securities.
Of the total offer, 40 billion lira worth of shares will be allocated to foreign investors, 20 billion lira to domestic institutional investors and the rest to individual investors.
Berdan Tekstil posted 441.1 billion lira net profits in 1996, up 670 percent from 1995's 57.3 billion lira. Net sales rose to 4.74 trillion lira last year from 2.61 trillion in 1995.
Company general manager Muhtesem Ekenler earlier said short-term debt would be repaid with income from the public offer.
He also said the company aimed to raise sales to 103 million marks this year from 85.6 million marks in 1996, including an export target of 50 million this year, after 38 million in 1996.

As an integrated plant with spinning, weaving, dyeing and finishing units and a product portfolio of polyviscose, including polyester, viscose, wool, linen and their blends, Berdan Tekstil has an annual output capacity of 13 million metres.
It plans to increase capacity to 15 million metres this year via a 12.5-million-mark modernisation investment.
